significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—"the number and representational proximity" of competitor facts predicts single-example recall failure—together with a form-(ii) mechanism in which suppressing a nearby competitor restores the correct answer. This fixes expectations beyond individual facts: higher "InterferenceLoad" should forecast more failures, and known-but-wrong outputs should preferentially match high-proximity competitors; that would materially refine the component-level account of factual recall studied by Geva et al. (2023) and the editable knowledge representations leveraged by MEMIT. Verified false and true are distinguishable, but the negative branch would mainly reject this representational-crowding account and its proposed measurable proxies rather than settle every explanation of inaccessible knowledge; the claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism if true. Topic-substitution check: replacing these specific competitor-load and intrusion claims with the generic knowledge-retrieval topic would not retain this score, because the predictive relation and causal error decomposition are the above-median contribution.

reach.justification: The named handles are "InterferenceLoad," a per-example failure predictor, and the "competitor-aware retrieval nudge," an inference-time intervention that suppresses an interfering direction. InterferenceLoad is ex ante because it is claimed to predict whether retrieval will succeed before the answer is produced, while the nudge supplies an action window during generation rather than merely explaining an observed error. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion still predicts a transferable relation—greater competitor count/proximity implies lower recall and more competitor intrusions—and the hypothesis is framed for LLMs generally, with asserted characterization across Pythia, Qwen2.5, and Llama-3 families; likely downstream users include model auditors and inference-system designers. Topic-substitution check: the broad topic alone supplies neither this forecast nor an intervention, so the reach score rests on claim-specific handles rather than the general importance of factual reliability.
